naturaephilosophy.c: NATURAE Philos ophy, is the lame with what is usually call’d Phystcks, vi%. That Science which contemplates the Powers of Nature, the Properties of Natural Bodies, and their mutual Action one upon another.

naviculareos.c: NAVLCULARE Os, called also Cymbiforme, is the third Bone in each Foot, in that part of it which immediately succeeds the Leg.

navigation.c: NAVIGATION, is the Art of Sailing, whereby the Mariner is instructed how to guide a Ship from one Port to another, the shortest and latest way, and in the (honest Time : And this is twofold; either Improper, Which is called Coasting, in which the Places are at no great distance one from another, and the Ship fails usually in sight of Land, and is within Soundings. Now for the Performance of this, there is required a good Knowledge of the Lands, the Utc of the Compass, the Lead, or Soundmg-line, and (itch Books as stutters, &c. Navigation Proper, is where the Voyage is performed in the Vast Ocean, out of light of all Land ; and here is ncceilary not only the Knowledge of the Lead, Ccmpajs, Sec. But the Master must be a thro’ Sailer or Artist, and understand well Mercators Charts, Azimuth and Am* plitude Ccmpafs, Log-IJne, and all good Instruments for Celestial Observations that can be used at Sea. And how to perform the several Ruts and Cafes of this Art, you will find under the Word Plain, and Mercators Sailing.

Wright’s , commonly called Mercatofs Chart, where the Meridians are increased in Proportion, as the Parallels shorten : That is, as the Secants of the Arks contained between the Point of Latitude, and the Equator. nebulousstars.c: NEBULOUS Stars, are certain Fixed Stars of a dull, j ale, and obscurilh Light.

necrosis.c: NECROSIS, is a Black and Blue Mark in any part of the Body.

negativeptegmnt.c: NEGATIVE Ptegmnt, is when an Action, Information, or such like, is brought against one, and the Defendant Pleads in Bar of the Action, or otherwise a Negative Plea, which is not to special an Answer to the Action, but that it includes also an Affirmative : As if a Man being impleaded to have done a thing on such a Day, or in such a Place, denieth that he did it Modo & forma dedamata ; which implieth nevertheless, That in some sort he did it : Or if a Man be said to have alienated Land in Fee, and he faith, he hath not alienated in Fee, this is Negative Pregnant ; for tho’ it be true that he hath not alienated in Fee, yet it may be, he hath made an Estate in Taile.

negativequantitiesinalgebra.c: NEGATIVE Quantities in Algebra, are such as have before them the NEGATIVE Sign —', and which are supposed to be less than nothing. These are directly contrary to Positive, Affirmative, or Real Quantities. NE in juse vexes, is a Writ which lies fora Tenant that is Distrained by his Lord for other Services than he ought to make, and is a Prohibition to the Lord in it self, commanding him not to Distrain.

neipetides.c: NEIPE TIDES, written also Nepe or Keep, are thole Tides (when the Moon is in the middle of the second and last Quarter) which arc opposite to the Spring-Tides ; and as the highest of the Spring-Tides is three Days after the Full or Change, so the lowest of the Neep is four N E 0__ Days before the Full or Change ; and then the Seamen say, that it is Deep Neipe : AHfo when a Ship wants Water, so that five cannot get out c> a Harbour, off from the Ground, or out of the Dock, the Seamen say she is Neipcd.

noctambulo.c: NOCTAMBULO, or NoBambulus, is one who walks in his Sleep.

nocturnal.c: NOCTURNAL, is an Instrument made of Box, Ivory, or Brais, divided on both sides, to take the Altitude or Depredion of rhe Pole-Star, in respect to the Pole it self, in order to find the Latitude, and nearly the Hour of the Night. NOCTURNAL A>\ , is that Space in the Heavens which the Sun, Moon, or stars, run thro’ from their Rising to their Setting.

nocturlabe.c: NOCTURLABE, is an Instrument used to find how much the North Star is higher er lower than the Pole at all Hours of the Night.

noctiluca.c: NOCTI Luce, is one of the two kinds of Phosphorus ; the former of which, such as the Bohemian Stcne, Hermetic 4 Phosphorus Baiduini, Ike. will not shine, except first exposed to rhe sunbeams, but this kind of Nciticula, is a lest-shining Substance, which requires the being exposed to no Light to render it Luminous: As the Phosphorus made of Urine, &c. which fee in Phosphorus. Mr. Boyle in his Book of the Aerial NoBiluca , reckons three of these Nocti succe. 1. The Gummous, Consistent or Constant one, (as some Germans call it) which is in the Form of a Consistent Body. 2. The Liquid NoBiluca, which probably is only the former dissolved in a proper Liquor. 3. The Aerial NoBiluca, because it would immediately begin to shine, on being exposed to the open Air. See the Process for this last, P. 1 o 5. of the aforementioned Book, which being much the same with that of the Phosphorus, commonly made out of Humane Urine, I have omitted. See Phosphorus.

nodes.c: NODES, in Astronomy, signifie the Points of Intersection of the Orbit of the Sun, or any Planet, with the Ecliptick; so that the Point where a Planet passes over the Ecliptick, out of Southern into Northern Latitude, is called the North Node : And where it descends from North to South,’tis the South-bWe; which Nodes (according to some) change their Places in the Zodiack, like the Planets: But Mr. Newton proves Prop. 14. Lib. 3. that the Nodes of all the Planets Orbits (as well as their Aphelia) are at Rest.

nodus.c: NODUS. One Method of which, Mr. Collins at the end of his Sector on a Quadrant, gives as follows. First, Draw an Horizontal Dyal for the Latitude proposed : Then by rhe help of the Sun’s Azimuth (which may be found by a Quadrant) or by knowing the Hour of the Day by that Horizontal Dyal, draw a true Meridian from the Hole or Nodus proposed, both above in the deling, and below on the Walls and Floor of the Room ; so that if a Right Line were extended from the said Hole or Nodus to any Point in any of those Lines, it would be in the Meridian Circle of the World. Next, six the ^end of a Thread in the Centre of the Hole or Nodus, and move the other end thereof up or down in the said Meridian drawn on the deling or Wall, until by applying the side of a Quadrant to that Thread, it is found to be elevated equal to the Latitude of the Place, then that Thread is directly situated parallel to the Axis of the World, and the Point where the end of that Thread toucheth the Meridian either on the Ceiling or Wall, is that Point in the direct Axis sought for; wherein six one end of the Thread, which Thread will be of present Use in projecting the Hour-Points in any place proposed. Then place the Centre of the Horizontal Dyal, in the Centre of the Hole or Nodus, and situate it exactly parallel to the Horizon, and its Meridian in the Meridian of the World, (which may easily be done, if at the Instant you know the true Hour of the Day) then take the Thread whose end is six’d in a Point in the direct Axe, and move it to and fro, until the Thread doth interpose between your Eye, and the Hour-Linc on the Horizontal Dyal, and keeping your Eye ■in that Position, make a Point, ’or Mark where you please, so that the Thread may interpose between that Point and your Eye ; which Point so found, will shew the true time of the Day at that Hour all the Year long, the Sun shining -thereon, so will rhe Point and the said Thread serve to shew the Hour, instead of an Hour line. In like manner, the Thread fixed in the Axis maybe again moved to and fro, until the Thread doth interpose between the Eye and any other Hour-Linc desired on the Horizontal Dyal, and then (as before) make another Point or Mark in any place at pleasure, by projecting a Point from the Eye, so that the Thread interpose between that Point to be made, and the Eye, so will that Point so found shew the true time of the Day for the seme Hour that the Hour-Line did on the Horizontal Dyal, which was shadow’d by the Thread. Thus you may proceed, (by the help of that Thread and the several Hour-Lincs on the Horizontal Dyal) to find the other Hour-Points, • which must have the seme Numbers let to them as the Hour-Liues on the Horizontal Dyal have. Otherwise to make a Dyal from a Hole in any Pane of Glass in the Window, and to graduate the Hour-Lincs on the Ceiling, Floor, Cse. Hole is supposed to be the Centre of the Horizontal Dyal, and being true placed, the Suse thereof, if supposed continued, will run into rite Point in the Meridian of the Cieling besets found, where a Thread is to be fixed ; then se one extend a Thread fastned in the Centre of tn Horizontal Dyal, parallel to the Horizon ove r each respective Hour-Line, and holding it dy, let another extend the Thread fastned in 1)1 Meridian in the Cieling, along by the xEdges ° the Horizontal Thread, which will find dh' es Points on the Ground, thro’ which, if Ho ur ' Lines be drawn,the Sun shining thro’ the Hose"" the Pane of Glass, will shew the Time of Hay. ■ , hc For the Points that will be thus found on 1 Beam or Transonic, the Thread fixed in c Cieling, or instead of it a piece of Tape tn f fixed must be moved so up and down, that Spot of the Sun may shine upon ir; and b c " ^ extended to the Transome or Beam, graiseatct with the Hour-Lines, it there shews the Tise c the Day. ^ Note, That ’twill be convenient to have 1 Pane of Glass darken’d, thro’ which 1 Spot is to shine. Large, Long, Breve, Semi-hreve, Minim, Crotchet, Quaver, Semi-quaver, and Demi-Semiquaver. The four first are usually termed Notes of Augmentation, or Increase, and the five last ot Diminution or Decrease. nuperobiit.c: NUPER Obi it , is a Writ that lies for a Coheir, being deforced by her Co-parcener of Lands or Tenements, whereof any of their Ancestors died seized of an Estate in Fee-simple.

nusance.c: NUSANCE, a Term in Law, signifying nor only a Thi^g done, whereby another Man is annoyed in his Free Lands or Tenements, but the Aliife or Writ which lieth for the same; and now generally, instead of this, is brought in Actions of Trespass.

nutrition.c: NUTRITION, is a Natural Increase, whereby that which continually decays of any Corporeal Substance, is repaired by convenient Nourishment. Dr. Havers, in his Osteologia, will not have Nutrition to be any Reparation of the Loss of the Substance of the Solid Parts ordinarily, but only a continual Succession and Supply of Spirits, and of all those Fluid Parts which fill the containing Parts, and keep them distended.

nux.c: NUX, is a sort of Pain in the Head, whiah afflicts a Place as big as a Nut; as an Ovum or Clavus is another sort, where the Scat of the Pain is larger.

nychthemeron.c: NYCHTHEMERON, is Four and twenty Hours Space, or an entire Day and Night.

nyctalopia.c: NYCTALOPIA is Two-fold : The First is a Dimness of the Sight in the Night, or in dark Places, without any Impediment in the Light. The Other is Dimness in the Light, and clear Sight in the Night, or in Shady Places.

nymph.c: NYMPHÆ, are little soft Pieces of Flesh,' arising from the Commissure of the Os pubis within the Vagina ; so called, because they stand near the Passage of the Water that comes out of the Bladder. Also the Hollowness or void Space in the Nether Lip is so called.

nymphotomy.c:
